title: Victorian Terrace To Eight-Bed Luxury Co-Living
desc: An eight-bedroom luxury co-living conversion inside a bay-fronted Victorian terrace in Southsea.

listing.provenance: By HMO Designers, part of Thistle Group

writeup.approach: The building is a bay-fronted Victorian terrace on A residential street with dormers already in the roof and shops either side. Inside, the communal floor runs open plan: kitchen, dining and living in one length on a herringbone floor, with the kitchen tucked along the far wall rather than closed off. That single decision is what makes co-living work here. Eight people sharing a corridor is a house share; eight people sharing a room this size is somewhere you would choose to live.
writeup.outcome: Complete, and the most recent of the practice's Portsmouth HMO projects.

summary: The conversion of a bay-fronted Victorian terrace in Southsea into an eight-bedroom luxury co-living house for professionals, working with the existing roof dormers.

The critical decision was where the kitchen went. Rather than isolating it, the scheme opens the communal floor into a single kitchen, dining and living space laid on herringbone flooring. Eight people sharing a corridor is a house share; eight people sharing a room this size is somewhere you'd choose to live.
HMO Designers, part of Thistle Group, designed the conversion and the interior scheme for the co-living accommodation.
The project is complete and was Highly Commended for Best Co-Living Space Design at the 2024 HMO Awards.
